budget_items.what_was_said: The presenter noted fines for non-compliance with the MS4 permit as a reason not to simply forgo compliance.
A rough estimate of the replacement value of the town's stormwater system (over 1,300 catch basins, ~550 outfalls, 50 miles of roadway infrastructure) was given.
A worked example showed how a commercial property with two equivalent residential units (ERUs) would be billed if the rate were set at a given amount per ERU.

budget_items.topic: Example fee structures in other Massachusetts towns
budget_items.what_was_said: Rutland was described as charging a flat fee for any property with impervious area; Chelmsford charges a flat fee for single/two-family homes and a tiered fee for other properties, with the largest payer cited.

Example properties in a neighboring community with a stormwater utility were shown, including a very large commercial property, a medium commercial property, and a small commercial property, to illustrate the range of fees under an ERU-based system.

budget_items.topic: Proposed small residential stormwater fee for Lunenburg
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force has been looking at a flat fee for small (one-to-two family) residential properties that would not exceed a stated cap, at least initially, with the fee possibly needing adjustment down the road as a new MS4 permit is issued.
The task force is considering a credit of up to a stated share of the assessed fee for properties managing their own stormwater on site, based on other Massachusetts communities' practice.

decisions.decision: Task force plans to bring the stormwater utility enabling legislation and bylaw to spring town meeting for approval, with the stormwater budget to follow at fall town meeting.
Fee collection under the proposed utility would not begin until a target future date, contingent on fall town meeting approving the storm water budget.
Task force agreed to make the FAQ document available in hard copy at locations such as the library, town hall, the Ritter building, and the adult activity center, in addition to the town website.

minutes.headline: Task force outlined a proposed stormwater utility fee; bylaw goes to spring town meeting, fees start later.
minutes.summary: An engineering consultant presented the Stormwater Task Force's plan for a stormwater utility to fund MS4 federal permit compliance, explaining how fees would be based on impervious surface area rather than property value. No fee, budget, or bylaw vote was taken at this meeting; the plan calls for the enabling legislation and bylaw to go before spring town meeting and the storm water budget before fall town meeting, with residents raising questions about state roads, tax-exempt and agricultural properties, and credit caps.

what_happened.line: Task force will bring stormwater utility enabling legislation and a bylaw to spring town meeting for a vote.
Fee collection would not start until after fall town meeting separately approves the stormwater budget.
Proposed fees would be based on a property's impervious surface area rather than its assessed value.
Residents asked whether state-maintained roads, tax-exempt and agricultural properties would pay the fee, and why a credit for on-site stormwater management is capped rather than full.
No fee, budget, or bylaw vote was taken at this meeting; it was presentation and discussion only.

why_it_matters: A vote at spring town meeting would create a new stormwater fee, billed by impervious surface area, separate from the property tax bill.
A second vote at fall town meeting would set the budget the fee actually funds, so residents get two separate decisions before any bill arrives.
Owners of large paved lots -- commercial, some agricultural -- would likely see a larger fee than most homes, where a capped flat fee is proposed.
